subject: pathology
title: Integrin Activation, Endothelial Transmigration, and Chemotaxis

steps.tx: Rolling leukocytes slow down and arrest firmly on the activated endothelial lining when low-affinity tethering switches to high-affinity adhesion. This firm arrest is mediated by heterodimeric cell-surface glycoproteins consisting of non-covalently linked alpha and beta chains known as **integrins**, expressed constitutively on leukocyte surfaces in low-affinity conformations.
steps.say: Integrins are heterodimeric leukocyte receptors that switch to high affinity to arrest rolling cells firmly.

steps.tx: As rolling neutrophils encounter chemokines displayed on the luminal endothelial surface, chemokine receptors trigger an intracellular signaling cascade termed inside-out signaling. This phosphorylation event induces a rapid allosteric conformational shift that converts the **beta-two integrin LFA-1** from a bent, low-affinity state into an extended, high-affinity ligand-binding conformation.
steps.say: Chemokines trigger inside-out signaling that straightens LFA-1 integrins into high-affinity conformations.

nodes.label: Rolling Neutrophil Binds Endothelial Proteoglycan-Bound Chemokine (CXCL8)
G-Protein-Coupled Receptor Triggers Intracellular Talin and Kindlin Recruitment
LFA-1 (CD11a/CD18) Unfolds from Inactive Bent to Extended High-Affinity State
High-Affinity LFA-1 Clamps Endothelial ICAM-1, Halting Rolling Instantly

steps.tx: High-affinity beta-two integrins on neutrophils bind specific counter-receptors belonging to the immunoglobulin superfamily expressed on activated endothelial cells. Most critically, leukocyte LFA-one and Mac-one bind **intercellular adhesion molecule-1 (ICAM-1)**, whose endothelial expression is massively upregulated by tumor necrosis factor and interleukin-one.
steps.say: Activated neutrophil integrins clamp endothelial ICAM-1, arresting the leukocyte firmly on the vessel wall.

left.title: Beta-2 Integrins (CD18 Family)
points: LFA-1 (CD11a/CD18): binds endothelial ICAM-1 and ICAM-2
Mac-1 (CD11b/CD18): binds ICAM-1 and complement fragment iC3b
Constitutively expressed on neutrophils, monocytes, and T-lymphocytes
Mutated or absent in leukocyte adhesion deficiency type 1

right.title: Beta-1 Integrins (VLA Family)
points: VLA-4 (CD49d/CD29, alpha-4-beta-1): binds endothelial VCAM-1
Expressed predominantly on monocytes, eosinophils, and lymphocytes
Directs non-neutrophilic recruitment in chronic inflammation and asthma
Targeted pharmacologically by monoclonal antibody natalizumab

steps.tx: High affinity beta 2 integrins on neutrophils grip immunoglobulin family receptors on activated endothelium. The critical pairing is leukocyte LFA 1 and Mac 1 with **ICAM 1**, whose endothelial display rises sharply under tumour necrosis factor and interleukin 1. That grip stops the rolling cell. Diapedesis is the next move: the leukocyte squeezes between endothelial cells of a postcapillary venule and enters the tissue, crawling along the chemotactic gradient that called it there.
steps.say: Neutrophil LFA 1 and Mac 1 lock onto endothelial ICAM 1, which tumour necrosis factor and interleukin 1 strongly increase. Firm adhesion ends the roll. The cell then crosses the postcapillary venule wall between endothelial cells and follows the chemical gradient into the tissue.

vis.alt: A leukocyte squeezing through the wall of a postcapillary venule into tissue along a chemotactic gradient.
vis.caption: After firm adhesion, a white cell passes between endothelial cells of a postcapillary venule and migrates into the tissue. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Following firm adhesion, leukocytes flatten out and migrate through the interendothelial junctions into the extravascular interstitium. Termed **diapedesis or transmigration**, this process occurs predominantly across postcapillary venules, driven by homotypic binding between platelet endothelial cell adhesion molecule-one molecules expressed on both leukocyte and endothelial borders.
steps.say: Diapedesis is leukocyte transmigration across interendothelial junctions mediated by PECAM-1.

vis.caption: Anterior chamber uveal inflammation illustrating intense vascular diapedesis and hypopyon formation.
vis.alt: Anterior uveitis demonstrating intense leukocyte transmigration into aqueous humor

steps.tx: To traverse the dense basement membrane underlying the endothelial monolayer, migrating leukocytes must digest extracellular matrix barriers. Adherent neutrophils secrete matrix metalloproteinases, specifically **collagenases and gelatinases**, which transiently dissolve type four collagen and laminin to permit smooth passage into the connective tissue.
steps.say: Neutrophils secrete collagenases that dissolve basement membrane type IV collagen during transmigration.

nodes.label: Leukocyte Squeezes Through PECAM-1 Sealed Interendothelial Junction
Encounters Dense Extracellular Scaffolding of Type IV Collagen and Laminin
Specific Granules Release Matrix Metalloproteinases (MMP-2 and MMP-9)
Enzymatic Focal Cleavage Opens Route into the Extravascular Stroma

steps.tx: Once in the extravascular connective tissue, leukocytes migrate directionally along a chemical concentration gradient toward the source of infection or tissue damage. This directed locomotion is **chemotaxis**, guided by both exogenous bacterial peptides and endogenous chemical attractants like complement fragment C5a, leukotriene B4, and chemokine interleukin-eight.
steps.say: Chemotaxis guides leukocytes along chemical concentration gradients toward the site of tissue injury.

left.title: Exogenous Chemotactic Factors
points: Bacterial formyl-methionyl peptides (N-formylmethionine, fMLP)
Conserved signature of prokaryotic bacterial protein initiation
Binds specific G-protein-coupled formyl peptide receptors (FPR1)
Directs leukocytes toward live dividing bacterial pathogens

right.title: Endogenous Chemotactic Factors
points: Complement fragment C5a generated during complement activation
Leukotriene B4 (LTB4) generated via 5-lipoxygenase pathway
Chemokines such as interleukin-8 (CXCL8) secreted by macrophages
Bind specific rhodopsin-like seven-transmembrane GPCRs

steps.tx: Binding of chemotactic agents to seven-transmembrane G-protein-coupled receptors activates small intracellular GTPases belonging to the Rho, Rac, and Cdc42 families. Rac stimulates actin polymerization to push forward a crawling **leading-edge pseudopod**, while Rho activates myosin phosphorylation at the trailing edge to retract the cell body.
steps.say: Rac polymerizes actin at the leading edge to extend pseudopods, while Rho contracts the trailing tail.

nodes.label: Chemoattractant Binds G-Protein-Coupled Receptor on Leukocyte Membrane
G-Beta-Gamma Subunits Activate Phosphoinositide 3-Kinase and Rac GTPase
Polymerization of G-Actin into F-Actin Pushes Leading Edge Pseudopod
Myosin Motors Contract Trailing Cell Body, Pulling Leukocyte Forward

steps.tx: The nature of the cellular infiltrate at an inflamed focus changes dynamically over time. During the initial six to twenty-four hours, **neutrophils predominate** because they are more abundant in blood and respond rapidly to chemokines, whereas monocytes replace neutrophils over twenty-four to forty-eight hours, transforming into long-lived tissue macrophages.
steps.say: Neutrophils arrive first within twenty-four hours, followed by monocytes that survive longer as macrophages.

left.title: Early Infiltrate: Neutrophils (6 to 24 Hours)
points: Represent 60-70% of circulating white blood cells in blood
Fast responders with high surface density of CXCR1/CXCR2 receptors
Short lifespan in tissue: undergo apoptosis within 24 to 48 hours
Specialize in rapid microbial killing via toxic granule discharge

right.title: Late Infiltrate: Monocytes / Macrophages (24 to 48 Hours)
points: Less abundant in blood; slower transendothelial migration velocity
Survive for weeks or months in tissue as differentiated macrophages
Phagocytose apoptotic neutrophils, cellular debris, and dead microbes
Secrete growth factors (VEGF, TGF-beta) to coordinate tissue repair
